name: TX-04
label: Safe R

key_factors: Pat Fallon holds a roughly 50-to-1 fundraising advantage; challenger Jason Pearce has about $2,000 on hand
The district leans about twelve points Republican, and Fallon has won it comfortably since 2020
Polymarket prices Pearce's win chance at only about 6 percent
No public polling or expert ratings, and no evidence of a serious Democratic operation
model.rationale: Every available signal points the same direction: a strongly Republican district, an incumbent with a seven-figure war chest against a challenger who has raised almost nothing, and markets pricing a near-certain Republican hold. That one-sided campaign environment justifies shading the expected margin slightly more Republican than the underlying fundamentals alone would indicate.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending against Fallon or an unforeseen scandal would be the only plausible route to a closer race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Texas's 4th District sits in heavily Republican northeast Texas, with a partisan lean of roughly twelve points toward the GOP. Pat Fallon, first elected in 2020, is seeking another term after easily securing renomination. The race has drawn no public polling and no expert ratings, so structural indicators carry the assessment.

The financial picture is stark. Fallon has raised about $790,000 and holds more than $1 million on hand, while Democrat Jason Pearce has raised roughly $16,000 with little cash remaining. Outside support has flowed only to Fallon. Prediction markets give Pearce about a six percent chance of winning. Nothing in the fundraising totals, the district's lean, or the incumbent's record suggests a competitive contest; the open question is the size of the winning margin, not which party prevails.
